P.O. Ramkunda, P.S. Ramkunda, District- Garhwa, Jharkhand ... ... Appellant  Versus The State of Jharkhand ...... Respondent

CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SUJIT NARAYAN PRASAD HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE NAVNEET KUMAR --------

For the Appellant : Mr. Surendra Pd. Sinha, Advocate For the State : Mr. Anup Pawan Topno, APP  --------
Order No. 03/ Dated: 10th January, 2025 1.

The instant appeal filed under Section 21 (4) of the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008, is directed against the order dated 07.10.2024 passed by the learned Additional Judicial Commissioner-IV- cum-Spl. Judge POCSO, Ranchi, in B.P. No. 1428 of 2024, by which the prayer for regular bail of the appellant in connection with Anti Human Trafficking Unit P.S. Case No. 4 of 2024, registered under Sections 363/370 of the Indian Penal Code, Section 75/81 of J.J. Act and Section 14/16 Child Labour Prohibition & Regulation Act, 1986, has been rejected..

sentences.text: 2. It has been contended on behalf of the appellant that this is the first offence said to be committed by the appellant who having the age of 24 years and student of intermediate class and belongs to a family of reputed, since, his father is running a cloth shop in the native village.

The learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that although the nature of the allegation against the appellant as has been alleged is serious so far as it relates to commission of forgery of Aadhaar Card is concerned but taking into the consideration, the age of the appellant and the present offence is the first offence,
having no criminal antecedent the case of the appellant may considered by giving a chance to amend himself.

It has further been contended that even the co-accused- namely, Uttam Kumar Keshri Raj Kumar Keshri vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155354359/
1 happens to be the brother of the present appellant has been directed to be enlarged on bail vide order dated 10.09.2024 passed by this Court in Cr. Appeal (DB) No.795 of 2024.

sentences.text:
It has further been submitted that the appellant is languishing in judicial custody since, 26.07.2024 and the charge have been framed but as no witnesses have been examined therefore, the prayer has been made to interfere with the impugned order so that the appellant may come out from the judicial custody and be able to carry out his study for the purpose of making his future.
3. While on the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and has submitted by making distinction in between case of the Uttam Kumar Keshri, appellant in Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 795 of 2024 wherein there is no allegation against the said appellant of commission of any forgery, while on the other hand against the present appellant, there is serious allegation of commission of forgery by fabricating the Aadhaar Card and that is the reason the charge has been framed under Sections 420, 467 & 468 of IPC and 363 and 370 thereof.
The learned State Counsel based upon the aforesaid grounds has submitted that it is therefore not a fit case to interfere with the impugned order.

4. This Court has heard the learned counsel for the parties and gone across the findings recorded by the learned trial court in the impugned order whereby and whereunder the prayer for regular bail of the appellant has been rejected.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant has relied upon the order passed by this Court in Cr.
Appeal(DB) No.795 of 2024 with respect to the co-accused, namely, Uttam Kumar Keshri who has been directed to be released on bail.
However, he himself submitted that the allegation against the present appellant is of fabrication of the Aadhaar Card.

6. This Court in order to appreciate the argument advanced on behalf of the appellant as also the State has gone through the content of the FIR and material collected during the course of the investigation as available in the case diary which has been called for by order dated 22.11.2024, and found that although the offence has been alleged to be committed under Sections 363 and 370 of IPC but it appears from the order passed with respect to the co-accused person, namely, Uttam Kumar Keshri that the minor who has been sought to be trafficked actually has not been trafficked since they have been got hold in the station itself.

7. So far as the allegation against the present appellant is concerned although the same pertains to the fabrication of the Aadhaar Card but 2 Cr. Appeal (D.B.) No. 1423 of 2024 considering the fact that the appellant is languishing in judicial custody since 26.07.2024, wherein the charge has been framed on 04.12.2024 but no witnesses has been examined as also the appellant is having no criminal antecedent as such, is of the view that the impugned order needs to be interfered with.
8. Accordingly, the order dated 07.10.2024 passed in B.P. No. 1428 of 2024 in connection with Anti Human Trafficking Unit P.S. Case No. 4 of 2024, is hereby quashed and set aside.
